engines.name: Master orchestration engine
engines.purpose: Turn a deployment objective into durable, bounded work across independent engines. It coordinates capabilities and policy without embedding a particular country, allegation, institution or desired conclusion.
engines.owns: Objectives, directives, work graphs, workflow definitions, tasks, attempts, agent definitions, agent runs, capability leases, checkpoints, budgets, active-work accounting and resumable execution.
engines.inputs: A versioned objective, authorized project scope, engine capability manifests, resource ceilings and explicit stop conditions.
engines.outputs: Task and run events, revision-bound artifacts, unresolved questions, cost and effort ledgers, dependency graphs and operator decision requests.
engines.events: task.ready, task.leased, task.completed, task.blocked, budget.threshold, run.paused
engines.runtime: Control worker with a durable PostgreSQL queue and transactional outbox. Workers lease jobs; tool brokers enforce scoped capability tokens. A model never receives a database administrator credential.
engines.limits: At-least-once execution with idempotent effects; bounded retries and no false promise of exactly-once external delivery. A model may propose tasks, while deterministic policy controls execution.
engines.visual: Objective map, task dependency graph, live swimlanes, agent activity, checkpoint inspection, cost meter and effort allocation chart.
engines.acceptance: Kill a worker after a side effect and before acknowledgment: recovery reconciles the effect without duplicating it. Pause revokes new leases. Budget exhaustion leaves recoverable work and visible reasons.

engines.name: Identity authorization and policy engine
engines.purpose: Provide reusable authorization decisions for users, services, agents, data and external actions. Reuse the existing intake identity boundary through federation or an adapter instead of introducing incompatible identities.
engines.owns: Tenant and project memberships, actor mappings, service identities, purpose grants, policy versions, compartment permissions, disclosure decisions, rate limits and revocation epochs.
engines.inputs: Authenticated identity, trusted tenant context, resource scope, requested action, purpose and applicable policy revision.
engines.outputs: Allow or deny decisions with reasons, redacted projections, short-lived capability grants and audit events.
engines.runtime: Shared typed library plus a service boundary where needed; server-side enforcement and database row policies form independent layers. Fail closed when policy cannot be evaluated.
engines.limits: Intake protected-identity dual control remains authoritative. An owner release decision does not override a participant restriction or disclose another tenant. Research access does not confer sending, purchasing or publishing authority.
engines.visual: Who can access this record, field-level disclosure preview, capability inspector and revocation impact view.
engines.acceptance: Cross-tenant reads fail through APIs, search, counts, exports, background jobs and caches. Expired or wrong-purpose grants cannot send, decrypt or publish.

engines.name: Secure intake and case workflow engine
engines.purpose: Accept reports, preserve the original account, manage case state and offer safe participant follow-up. Reuse the existing upstream engine as its own versioned product.
engines.owns: Versioned intake forms and submissions, case IDs, participant credentials, protected identity compartments, queues, assignment, deadlines, referrals, review and case workflow state.
engines.inputs: Deployment manifests, submitted narratives, optional identity/contact preferences, file uploads and consent selections.
engines.outputs: Submission and case references, safe participant status/messages, authorized evidence references and signed integration events.
engines.api: Adapter operations createIntake, readCaseProjection, listEvidenceReferences, postParticipantMessage, transitionCase and acknowledgeEvent. Actual upstream routes are mapped in a compatibility manifest after contract discovery.
engines.runtime: Pinned upstream container, its worker and dedicated logical database. Core services use scoped APIs; they never write intake tables or impersonate a participant session.
engines.limits: Current protected-field encryption does not automatically protect binary files. Current participant surfaces do not imply arbitrary document sharing or message attachments. Each expansion requires a generic upstream change and contract tests.
engines.visual: Resumable form, participant portal, triage board, case timeline, protected-field badges and referral history.
engines.acceptance: A person can submit without paying or naming a lawyer, save a recovery secret, upload into quarantine, obtain a safe status and complete permitted follow-up without exposure of internal notes.

engines.name: Correspondence and outreach engine
engines.purpose: Resolve factual questions through authentic, concise communication with people likely to know. Provide an ordinary email workspace in which the human and authorized agents share control transparently.
engines.owns: Mailboxes, sender identities, contacts, contact provenance, questions, conversations, message versions, attachments, delivery attempts, sync cursors, suppression lists and control epochs.
engines.inputs: An unresolved question, relevance-ranked candidate contacts, minimum necessary context, allowed disclosure and a sending grant.
engines.outputs: Outbound inquiry, incoming response, attributed answer assertion, delivery evidence, refusal or no-response status and verification tasks.
engines.runtime: Mailbox API module plus isolated provider sync and delivery workers. OAuth credentials reside in a secret vault and are released only to the gateway, never to research agents.
engines.limits: Truthful branded automated identity; no invented scholarly affiliation, forged persona or hidden tracking pixels. Refusal stops follow-up. Sensitive witness contact uses the chosen safe channel and permission.
engines.visual: Three-pane inbox, thread timeline, question checklist, draft preview, visible automation status, takeover control and answer-to-evidence links.
engines.acceptance: Takeover before send dispatch fences all queued automated messages. A send already accepted by a provider remains visibly in transit. A duplicated inbound webhook creates one message and one answer extraction.

engines.name: Discovery and acquisition engine
engines.purpose: Find collections, records and potential witnesses, then acquire permitted public or authorized material with reproducible coverage accounting.
engines.owns: Source registry, connector configurations, query plans, retrieval jobs, pagination cursors, collection snapshots, access terms, refresh policies and acquisition receipts.
engines.inputs: Research questions, scope constraints, registered connectors, approved domains or archives and rate and byte ceilings.
engines.outputs: Candidate source records, captured bytes or metadata-only leads, professional contact leads, coverage maps and explicit blocked or unavailable items.
engines.runtime: Connector workers with bounded egress, SSRF controls, parser sandboxing, respectful retry policy and checkpointed collection traversal.
engines.limits: No authentication bypass or assumption that a visible link grants republication rights. Failed fetches remain leads, not preserved evidence. A changed URL or mirror is not independent corroboration.
engines.visual: Repository atlas, collection coverage, retrieval queues and side-by-side snapshots showing added, changed and missing records.
engines.acceptance: Resume a paginated collection after a crash without missing or double-counting entries. Record actual bytes acquired separately from discovered URLs and document-only metadata.

engines.name: Evidence storage and provenance engine
engines.purpose: Preserve originals and their history, support precise citations and make transformations auditable across research and production.
engines.owns: Evidence objects, content versions, acquisition and handling records, manifests, checksums, storage references, custody events, derivation edges, retention and integrity checks.
engines.inputs: Accepted acquisitions, clean intake attachments, original correspondence and authorized imported evidence bundles.
engines.outputs: Immutable version references, content-verified working copies, page or time selectors, custody exports and integrity alerts.
engines.runtime: Private versioned object storage plus metadata in PostgreSQL. Intake originals remain intake-owned; the adapter records source references and any authorized copies as new handling events.
engines.limits: SHA-256 demonstrates byte consistency, not that a recording is genuine or that its account is true. Storage ETags are not substituted for evidence hashes. Storage provider retention semantics must be tested.
engines.visual: Original and derivative tree, acquisition timeline, document viewer, checksum verification results and redaction overlays.
engines.acceptance: A restored original matches its retained digest. Mutated bytes are detected. An old citation opens the exact preserved version, and a missing original displays a provenance gap.

engines.name: Document and media processing engine
engines.purpose: Convert text, scans, audio and video into searchable, inspectable derivatives while preserving uncertainty and alignment to originals.
engines.owns: Processing specifications, OCR/transcript/translation revisions, language metadata, page geometry, speaker segments, timebase maps and quality observations.
engines.inputs: Authorized evidence version, selected pipeline, language hints, provider policy and processing budget.
engines.outputs: Searchable text, time-aligned transcript, translation, thumbnails, redacted working copies and structured extraction proposals.
engines.runtime: Sandboxed CPU/GPU workers and replaceable local or remote model adapters. Sensitive data can be restricted to local processing; provider transmission is an explicit data use.
engines.limits: Original speech is retained alongside normalized text. Speaker labels are provisional and do not identify a person without evidence. OCR or machine translation cannot silently overwrite an original.
engines.visual: Original-text alignment, waveform transcript editor, translated parallel text and quality heatmap with selectable spans.
engines.acceptance: A corrected word preserves prior text and invalidates dependent claims. PDF coordinates and media timestamps round-trip to the correct original segment.

engines.name: Knowledge and verification engine
engines.purpose: Represent what is claimed, what supports or challenges it and what remains uncertain. Make source dependence and revision history explicit.
engines.owns: Entities, event intervals, relationships, claim revisions, evidence links, source families, alternative hypotheses, contradiction records, identity-resolution decisions and verification assessments.
engines.inputs: Extracted passages, attributed replies, structured reports and proposed entity or claim matches.
engines.outputs: Versioned claim dossiers, corroboration and challenge links, disputed entity matches, research gaps, graph views and correction impact sets.
engines.runtime: Relational canonical records, adjacency tables and indexed search. Optional graph projection is disposable and always authorization-filtered. Vector search is a retrieval aid, never a truth database.
engines.limits: Separate epistemic assessment, source genre, procedural/legal posture and editorial approval. No numerical guilt score. Repetition, rank or employment alone cannot establish personal involvement.
engines.visual: Evidence graph with supports/challenges/derived-from edges, event timeline, claim comparison and source independence view.
engines.acceptance: Copies of one report count as one source family. A contradicted claim remains visible with its contrary material. Entity merges are reversible and preserve aliases.

engines.name: Factual investigation engine
engines.purpose: Plan and conduct an inquiry from a report or research question through findings, using documentary work and outreach as equal tools.
engines.owns: Investigation plans, question trees, hypotheses, lead assessments, interview plans, verification checklists, closure criteria, finding revisions and referral recommendations.
engines.inputs: A case or scoped objective, evidence currently available, urgency, contact constraints and resource allocation.
engines.outputs: Prioritized questions, research and contact tasks, tested answers, findings, remaining uncertainties, possible next steps and reviewable investigation packages.
engines.runtime: Domain logic creates tasks executed by E00 and calls E03/E04/E07 through contracts. Its case reference does not duplicate the authoritative intake case lifecycle.
engines.limits: Investigate a report without declaring it true at intake. Inability to verify produces an unresolved assessment. Documentation may establish events without establishing individual criminal liability.
engines.visual: Question tree, hypothesis matrix, lead board, interview schedule, coverage and missing-evidence map, findings timeline.
engines.acceptance: A case cannot be called complete while material questions are silently skipped. Completion records answers, efforts, unavailable sources, contradictions, review decisions and reopening triggers.

engines.name: Editorial and story development engine
engines.purpose: Turn research into clear, compelling factual and artistic work with a traceable distinction between documented experience and creative choices.
engines.owns: Creative briefs, series, treatments, story arcs, scenes, beats, script and lyric revisions, viewpoint decisions, shot concepts and factual story links.
engines.inputs: Claim revisions, testimony-use permissions, desired medium, audience, editorial aim and constraints.
engines.outputs: Treatments, scripts, storyboards, shot plans, lyrics, narration, sound concepts and an assertion-to-source ledger.
engines.runtime: Creative workflow module with model adapters and an editor. Templates are generic; deployments provide subject matter and branding.
engines.limits: Use attributed testimony for private thoughts when available. Reconstruction, composites, inferred feelings and invented dialogue are declared. Generated images cannot masquerade as archival evidence.
engines.visual: Story map, evidence-linked script, shot cards, character perspective timeline and factual versus artistic layer toggles.
engines.acceptance: Selecting a factual line reveals its exact evidence and uncertainty. Changing a claim marks affected beats and scripts stale without rewriting approved text invisibly.

engines.name: Media production engine
engines.purpose: Create, edit, render and package finished works across media through reusable production jobs and interchangeable tool adapters.
engines.owns: Asset revisions, renditions, media projects, timelines, shot lists, audio stems, compositions, captions, render graphs, tool versions and quality reports.
engines.inputs: Approved or draft-labeled story revisions, rights decisions, original assets, production constraints and render budgets.
engines.outputs: Films, audio programs, music, images, animation, written layouts, interactive packages, exhibitions and interoperable project files.
engines.runtime: Isolated render workers, CPU/GPU pools, temporary workspaces and a provider-neutral adapter protocol for generation, editing and assembly. No promise of pixel-identical reproduction from stochastic external tools.
engines.limits: Retain exact output bytes, input revisions, seeds where available and provider/tool versions. Performance, voice and likeness permissions are separate from factual permission. New media use an extension contract.
engines.visual: Shot and edit timeline, waveform, storyboard, asset dependency graph, render progress, source-linked preview and quality comparisons.
engines.acceptance: A complete pilot film, audio work, still image, written piece and interactive work render from manifests. Corrections identify every dependent rendition and export.

engines.name: Consent rights and use decisions engine
engines.purpose: Control allowed uses of identities, testimony, originals, derivatives and performances while keeping factual research separate from reproduction permissions.
engines.owns: Consent records, license terms, use requests, scope conditions, attribution requirements, term/territory/audience restrictions, withdrawals and review decisions.
engines.inputs: Participant choices, contributor agreements, source terms, proposed asset use and deployment policy.
engines.outputs: Purpose-specific allow/deny/review outcomes, required attribution, permitted derivatives, expiry notifications and impact notices.
engines.runtime: Policy module integrated with E01 and artifact lineage. Original permission evidence is versioned and compartmented.
engines.limits: Citation metadata disclosure, quotation, reproduction, adaptation, model processing and public identity are distinct uses. A public URL is not a universal license. A legal assessment is attributed and scoped to the applicable jurisdiction.
engines.visual: Rights matrix, consent timeline, release readiness, territory and term restrictions, and downstream withdrawal impact.
engines.acceptance: Unknown image reproduction rights block the image use without automatically suppressing permissible bibliographic citation. Withdrawal stops future unauthorized use and flags existing distributions.

engines.name: Packaging release and correction engine
engines.purpose: Prepare private evidence and media packages, and publish only the exact approved projection when the owner authorizes a specific release.
engines.owns: Export specifications, release candidates, signed approval manifests, dissemination receipts, recipients, source companions, corrections, withdrawals and supersession records.
engines.inputs: Selected artifact revisions, disclosure and rights decisions, recipient/channel/audience, owner authorization and purpose.
engines.outputs: Private review bundles, professional evidence packages, licensed deliveries, optional public reference pages and revision-aware correction notices.
engines.runtime: Private build worker and separate narrowly privileged delivery gateway. Public publisher is disabled and has no destination credentials until configured.
engines.limits: A model cannot decide that a justice process failed or that public disclosure is necessary. Authorization is bound to hashes, destination, audience and expiry. Corrections can flag urgency but cannot create an unapproved new disclosure.
engines.visual: Exact audience preview, redaction diff, dependency and permission matrix, owner decision record, release timeline and recipient delivery state.
engines.acceptance: Any change in content, rights, audience or source revision invalidates the affected candidate. Private originals are absent from public bytes, thumbnails, captions, metadata and search indexes.

engines.name: Resources and commercial operations engine
engines.purpose: Make sustained investigation and creative production financially and operationally manageable while supporting reuse by other organizations.
engines.owns: Project budgets, resource reservations, effort entries, contributor agreements, expenses, license products, invoices, revenue allocations and reconciliation records.
engines.inputs: Task usage, supplier rates, contracts, approved spending limits and distribution receipts.
engines.outputs: Cost forecasts, variance alerts, contribution records, license obligations, royalty or revenue statements and accounting exports.
engines.runtime: Business module with external billing/accounting adapters. Monetary values use integer minor units and explicit currency; transactions are idempotent and audited.
engines.limits: No payment is required to report wrongdoing. Payment and popularity do not change evidence assessments. Production expenditure, licensing sales and professional deployment contracts need explicit commercial authority.
engines.visual: Budget burn, forecast by medium, lane effort, contributor obligations and revenue reconciliation.
engines.acceptance: A replayed invoice webhook creates no duplicate payment or income record. An over-budget render is paused or uses a previously authorized smaller plan with visible tradeoffs.

engines.name: Visual workspace and audit engine
engines.purpose: Make the entire suite inspectable and operable through linked visual views, with equivalent accessible text and tables.
engines.owns: View definitions, saved filters, audit projections, dashboard layouts, event subscriptions, evidence-linked decision summaries and operational telemetry projections.
engines.inputs: Authorized engine projections, event streams, provenance edges, selected resource and user role.
engines.outputs: Navigable workbench, read models, dashboards, trace views, redacted audit bundles and alert panels.
engines.runtime: React/TypeScript interface, typed view-model API and authorization-filtered projections. Each engine ships a view manifest and fallback table schema.
engines.limits: Do not display hidden record counts, labels or topology that reveal protected material. Model decision summaries contain evidence and actions, not hidden chain-of-thought. Audit logs omit sensitive payloads.
engines.visual: Inbox, intake and case boards, source atlas, evidence viewer, graph, task canvas, studio, rights dashboard, release console and operations map.
engines.acceptance: Every actionable state has a visible explanation and drill-down. Keyboard users can complete the same workflows; graph relationships have accessible table equivalents and stale projections show timestamps.
